title: Applicability Determination
description: Determine and document whether the organization is a public community water system with more than 500 service connections and is subject to Water Quality Accountability Act requirements.

title: Compliance Responsibility
description: Assign accountable personnel for WQAA compliance activities, including operational, cybersecurity, asset management, certification, and reporting responsibilities.

title: Compliance Calendar
description: Maintain a compliance calendar covering valve inspections, hydrant testing, cybersecurity updates, annual certification, capital improvement reporting, and required submissions.

title: Evidence Repository
description: Maintain evidence that supports WQAA compliance, including inspection records, testing records, cybersecurity artifacts, asset management plans, certifications, and reports.

title: Executive Oversight
description: Provide executive oversight for WQAA compliance and ensure management reviews significant operational, cybersecurity, asset condition, and reporting risks.

title: Valve Inventory
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Maintain an inventory of valves in the public water system, including valve location, size, accessibility, operational condition, and inspection status.

title: Valve Inspection Schedule
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Inspect valves on the required WQAA schedule, including valves 12 inches or larger at least once every four years and all other covered valves at least once every eight years.

title: Valve Access Clearing
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Clear the area around each inspected valve to ensure full access for operational purposes.

title: Valve Box Cleaning
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Clean out valve boxes during required inspections so valves remain accessible and operable.

title: Valve Dynamic Testing
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Perform dynamic testing of inspected valves by opening and closing the valve using manufacturer guidance or the required percentage of total turns.

title: Valve Repair
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Repair or replace any valve found to be broken, inaccessible, or otherwise not operational.

title: Hydrant Inventory
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Maintain an inventory of fire hydrants in the public water system, including ownership, identifying marks, location, testing status, and maintenance records.

title: Annual Hydrant Testing
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Test every fire hydrant in the system at least annually to determine working condition.

title: Hydrant Flushing Plan
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Maintain and implement a plan for flushing every fire hydrant and every dead end of a main in the public water system.

title: Hydrant Ownership Marking
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Mark each owned or jointly owned hydrant with the purveyor name, abbreviation, corporate symbol, or other durable identifying mark.

title: Hydrant Location Marking
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Mark each hydrant with a number, symbol, or other identifier that allows the hydrant location to be determined from official records.

title: GPS Location Mapping
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Identify, to the extent possible, the geographic location of each valve and fire hydrant using GPS or other location technology.

title: Field Record Retention
category: VH - Valves, Hydrants, and Field Records
description: Retain inspection, test, and flushing records for valves and hydrants for at least 12 years.

title: Cybersecurity Program
description: Develop, maintain, and implement a cybersecurity program that defines oversight, accountabilities, responsibilities, policies, plans, processes, and procedures for managing cyber risk to the public water system.

title: Framework Alignment
description: Align the cybersecurity program to an accepted framework, such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Controls, or the ISO/IEC 27000 family of standards.

title: Cyber Program Update
description: Review and update the cybersecurity program when required by WQAA, NJCCIC guidance, material system changes, incidents, or significant changes in the threat environment.

title: NJCCIC Submission
description: Submit the developed or revised cybersecurity program to the New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell as required.

title: NJCCIC Membership
description: Maintain membership in the New Jersey Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell and use it as the designated coordination point for cybersecurity information sharing and reporting.

title: Cyber Insurance
description: Purchase and maintain cybersecurity insurance coverage as required by WQAA amendments.

title: Critical System Scope
description: Identify systems in scope for cybersecurity oversight, including industrial control systems, SCADA or operational systems, and customer information systems containing personal information.

title: Critical System Inventory
description: Maintain and annually review an inventory of critical systems and document changes that affect the cybersecurity program scope.

title: Cyber Risk Assessment
description: Assess and prioritize cyber risks to identified systems at least annually, including vulnerabilities, current threats, physical risks, disaster recovery, and business continuity considerations.

title: Risk Methodology
description: Document the risk assessment methodology and criteria used to assess, prioritize, and accept or remediate cybersecurity risks.

title: Risk Controls
description: Implement administrative, technical, physical, and compensating controls to mitigate prioritized cybersecurity risks to acceptable levels.

title: Risk Review
description: Review the cybersecurity risk assessment methodology at least annually and incorporate needed revisions.

title: Log Monitoring
description: Monitor log files for critical systems on a regular and consistent basis based on identified risk.

title: Threat Monitoring
description: Monitor internal and external sources of cyber threat and vulnerability information, including vendor, ISAC, ISAO, NJCCIC, and other relevant advisories.

title: Threat Applicability
description: Maintain a review process to determine whether threat and vulnerability information applies to the water system and what response is required.

title: Patch Review
description: Review vendor security patches in a timely manner and implement applicable patches or compensating controls based on risk.

title: Incident Process
description: Create and maintain a cybersecurity incident reporting process for cyber incidents, suspicious activity, and unusual cyber activity affecting the water system.

title: NJCCIC Reporting
description: Promptly report cybersecurity incidents to NJCCIC and follow applicable NJCCIC, BPU, and regulatory reporting formats and timelines.

title: ICS Unauthorized Access
description: Report cyber events involving unauthorized access to an industrial control system or authorized users exceeding their access.

title: Unauthorized Code
description: Report discovery of unauthorized programs, information, code, or commands on an industrial control system.

title: Cyber Extortion
description: Report threats, extortion attempts, or demands involving damage to the integrity or availability of industrial control systems, data, programs, systems, or information.

title: PII Breach Coordination
description: Coordinate and document required notifications for breaches involving customer personal information under applicable New Jersey law.

title: Response Recovery Plan
description: Maintain a cybersecurity incident response and recovery plan covering identification, response, recovery, escalation, communications, and evidence preservation.

title: Forensic Log Retention
description: Define and implement log file retention protocols that support cybersecurity investigations and forensic analysis.

title: Response Exercise
description: Exercise the cybersecurity incident response and recovery plan at least once every 24 calendar months using a tabletop exercise, functional exercise, or actual incident.

title: Lessons Learned
description: Document lessons learned after incident response exercises or actual cyber incidents and update the response and recovery plan as appropriate.

title: Awareness Program
description: Develop and implement a cybersecurity awareness program that covers general cybersecurity topics and emerging threats.

title: Awareness Review
description: Review the cybersecurity awareness program at least every two years and update it as appropriate.

title: Awareness Communications
description: Provide periodic cybersecurity awareness communications throughout the year.

title: Role-Based Training
description: Provide cybersecurity training that explains roles and responsibilities for personnel with access to industrial control systems and administrators of customer information systems containing personal information.

title: New Personnel Training
description: Maintain protocols for cybersecurity training of new personnel and periodic refresher training.

title: NOV Trigger Monitoring
description: Monitor notices of violation to identify when WQAA mitigation planning is triggered by three notices for any reason or two notices involving maximum contaminant level exceedances within a 12-month period.

title: Mitigation Plan
description: Submit a mitigation plan within 60 days after the applicable notice of violation trigger, specifying whether the issue will be addressed by operational changes or capital expenditure.

title: Mitigation Schedule
description: Include an implementation schedule in the notice of violation mitigation plan.

title: Technical Analysis
description: Support the mitigation plan with a technical analysis prepared by the licensed operator and professional engineer explaining how recurrence will be prevented.

title: Capital Integration
description: Incorporate required capital expenditures from notice of violation mitigation plans into the asset management plan.

title: Annual Certification
description: Prepare annual executive certification of compliance with federal and State drinking water regulations, WQAA operational requirements, cybersecurity program requirements, and infrastructure improvement requirements.

title: Authorized Certifier
description: Ensure the annual certification is signed by the responsible corporate officer, executive director, mayor, chief executive officer, or other applicable authorized official.

title: Certification Submission
description: Submit the annual WQAA certification to the Department of Environmental Protection and, if applicable, the Board of Public Utilities.

title: Website Posting
description: Post the annual WQAA certification, including cybersecurity program certification information, on the purveyor's internet website where required.

title: Audit Readiness
description: Maintain complete, accurate, and reviewable support for annual certifications to support DEP audit requests and avoid false or misleading certification risk.

title: Asset Management Plan
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Implement an asset management plan designed to inspect, maintain, repair, and renew water system infrastructure consistent with American Water Works Association standards.

title: Water Main Renewal
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Maintain a water main renewal program designed to achieve a 150-year replacement cycle or another justified cycle based on engineering analysis of asset condition and service life.

title: Treatment Program
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Maintain a water supply and treatment program to inspect, maintain, repair, renew, and upgrade wells, intakes, pumps, and treatment facilities.

title: Regulatory Alignment
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Ensure asset management and treatment programs align with applicable federal and State drinking water regulations, American Water Works Association standards, and mitigation plan commitments.

title: Priority Funding
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Dedicate funds annually to address and remediate the highest-priority projects identified in the asset management plan.

title: Plan Certification
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Certify asset management plans and system condition reports through the licensed operator or professional engineer and the applicable responsible executive official.

title: Capital Report
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Submit the required capital improvement report identifying infrastructure improvements completed, planned, and associated costs.

title: Ten-Year Outlook
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Include completed, planned, and costed capital improvements from the prior year and over the next 10 years in annual capital improvement reporting.

title: Municipal DCA Filing
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: For municipal water departments or municipal water authorities, submit required asset management or capital improvement reports to the Division of Local Government Services in the Department of Community Affairs.

title: Portal Submission
category: AM - Asset Management and Capital Planning
description: Submit required reports electronically through the centralized portal when available, while maintaining the obligation to submit even if the portal is not available.

title: Report Card Support
category: RC - State Review and Audit Readiness
description: Maintain records and evidence needed to support NJDEP report card review of compliance with drinking water quality standards, WQAA requirements, and other relevant factors.

title: Certification Audit Support
category: RC - State Review and Audit Readiness
description: Maintain audit-ready support for annual certifications and respond to DEP audit requests, including requests following late, missing, false, or misleading certifications.
